# The Mꜣ file: from ma to the temple it became
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Mꜣ** stay *ma*.

Mꜣ has no independent mythic biography because it is the principle that makes biography possible. It appears in every major Egyptian funerary and royal text as the standard against which lives, deeds, and even gods are measured. Its personification, Mꜣꜥt, sits in the solar barque and stands at the throne of every legitimate king. In Spell 125 of the Book of the Dead, the deceased enters the Hall of the Two Truths and declares before Osiris and the forty-two assessors that he has not committed theft, murder, falsehood, or any of the sins that disturb mꜣꜥt.  His heart is placed on the scales opposite the feather of Mꜣꜥt.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Mꜣ
- **ASCII form:** ma
- **Meaning:** "Truth, rightness, correctness, measure. Root of Maat (mꜣꜥt), the cosmic principle of truth and order"
- **Domain of influence:** Truth, Rightness, Correctness, Measure
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𓌴𓏤
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 142 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Mꜣ** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *ma* and **Mꜣ** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Mꜣ** lives at [/sites/ma/](/sites/ma/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ma/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ma/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ma/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Mꜣ** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Legal, Justice & Compliance** — The root of Maat; measure and rightness itself.
- **Architecture & Spatial Design** — The set-square and plummet that make a wall true; measure as the root of rightness.
- **Software, Cloud & Developer Infrastructure** — Correctness and measure; the two properties every test suite is hired to prove.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Egyptian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
